ModMetaData.name: Auto-hunt Manager
ModMetaData.author: alite
ModMetaData.description:
This is a manager for hunting that was inspired by the vanilla auto-slaughter manager. Its menu is accessed using the bow icon next to the wildlife tab, and through it you can specify things like what animals you want to cull, how much raw meat to try to store, and what counts as stored meat. Once set, the manager will check the available raw meat and if it isn't enough, the manager starts searching.
This manager will prioritize trying to find corpses or raw food that haven't been claimed, then it starts looking through the living wildlife to see if any of them can be culled down to the limits you specify. It will start with the animals least likely to retaliate (i.e. rabbits and squirrels), and gradually work up to hunting the most dangerous animals listed for hunting until either the nutrition level or the limits are met.
You can also specify some animals to be always hunted down to the specified levels using the Force column, which will cause the auto-hunt manager to cull those animals before it looks at nutrition or considers retaliation chance. It's mostly intended for allowing you to ensure insects are always hunted even if they aren't considered viable food, or for ensuring predators don't stick around on the map for too long.
Animals marked for taming will never be marked for hunting by the manager, and every time it marks an animal for hunting, that animal is put on an ignore list so it won't try to mark the animal for hunting again if you unmark it.
If you move your colony (i.e. via abandonment or gravship), then the manager will attempt to port over its settings to your new home. It is recommended that you double-check your configurations post settling as this loading sometimes doesn't work as intended, especially if you have something that enables multiple colony maps. This saving can be disabled in the menu, and does not matter if your colony never moves.
Because the map itself is what keeps track of this, adding or removing this mod mid-save will cause issues. Your save may survive those issues, but I wouldn't recommend testing fate.
Wild people are not included by this manager, and that is intentional.
